mutants.reason: Opcode check inverted: a correct AccessAck/AckData response gives PSLVERR=1 and PRDATA=0, and a wrong opcode is not flagged.
Setup is detected in non-IDLE states instead of IDLE, so a legal Setup never launches a request or completes a local error.
REQ leaves on a_ready=0 instead of 1, so channel A drops before acceptance and is held after the handshake.
The WAIT term is inverted: a response in WAIT is not counted, so the transfer hangs, and orphan d_valid in IDLE is counted.
A counted response no longer raises PREADY, so the APB transfer never completes.
PREADY resets to 1 instead of 0, so it is high while reset is asserted.
d_ready is driven to 0 after reset release instead of staying 1, so it never goes high and responses are not accepted.
Local-error branch is inverted: an illegal Setup gets no PREADY/PSLVERR, and other cycles get a spurious local error.
a_valid resets to 1, so o_tlul_a_valid is high during reset.
Source check inverted: a correct d_source gives PSLVERR and a wrong source is accepted as good.
Alignment test is inverted: aligned accesses are treated as illegal and misaligned ones launch a TL-UL request.
In REQ with a_ready the next state is inverted: a same-cycle response goes to WAIT (and then never arrives), and no response sends it to IDLE.
The load is qualified by a non-IDLE state, so a launch in IDLE never loads or starts a request.
A local error no longer raises PREADY, so the illegal transfer does not complete in the first Access cycle.
The default PSLVERR next value is 1, so PSLVERR is high without PREADY and on good completions.
The local-error test in the IDLE branch is inverted: the FSM goes to DONE on a non-Setup idle cycle (blocking the next Setup), and an illegal Setup stays in IDLE.
reg_a_rd resets to 1, so o_tlul_a_opcode is 3'b100 in reset instead of 0.
The response completion is qualified by a non-BUSY state, so a response in BUSY gives no PREADY, and a response in other states gives a spurious one.
Request payload (opcode, address, data) loads when there is no launch instead of on it, so channel A carries wrong or stale values.
a_valid next value is inverted: it is low when a request is presented and high when idle.
A local error completes with PSLVERR=0 instead of 1.
The default PREADY next value is 1, so PREADY is high on every cycle without a completion.
APB FSM reset polarity is inverted: the FSM is held in IDLE while running and takes the next state while in reset, so transfers are not processed and reset does not clear state.
d_ready resets to 1, so o_tlul_d_ready is high during reset.
The strobe test is inverted: full-strobe writes are rejected and partial-strobe writes launch a request.
In WAIT the response branch is inverted: the FSM returns to IDLE with no response, and stays in WAIT after the response.
The REQ-state term is inverted: a same-cycle response during acceptance is not counted, and a response outside REQ is counted.
PSLVERR resets to 1, so it is high without PREADY during reset.
Completion-register reset polarity is inverted: outputs are not cleared in reset and are held at 0 while running, so no completion appears.
TL-UL FSM reset polarity is inverted: it is held in IDLE during normal operation, so no request is ever presented, and reset does not clear it.
The completion condition is negated, so a normal response gives no completion and PREADY/PSLVERR/PRDATA are loaded with garbage on other cycles.
The IDLE branch moves to REQ when there is no launch instead of on a launch, so spurious requests start and legal ones do not.
The APB IDLE branch goes to BUSY when there is no launch instead of on a legal launch, so legal transfers stay in IDLE and idle cycles enter BUSY.
Reset polarity of a_valid/d_ready is inverted: they are cleared while running and set in reset, so there is no request and d_ready is 0 in operation.
BUSY goes to DONE when there is no response instead of on one, so the APB FSM leaves BUSY early and misses the real completion.
Payload-register reset polarity is inverted: opcode, address and data are not cleared in reset and are held at 0 while running, so requests have wrong content.
